AnalysisSide.description:
Which side of a change a piece of evidence belongs to.

Base-side evidence is hash-verified at analysis time and historical by
construction; it is labeled as base so a reader never mistakes it for the
current snapshot's content.
AnalysisSide.title: AnalysisSide

AnalysisStateRef.description:
One side of a change: the ref the caller asked for and what it resolved
to.

The base side carries no snapshot ID — it is reconstructed in memory or read
from Git objects, never a stored active snapshot. The target side carries
the active snapshot ID it was analyzed against, so a reader can tell exactly
which snapshot the analysis is bound to.
AnalysisStateRef.title: AnalysisStateRef

ChangeAnalysisKind.description: Which form of diff an analysis compares.
ChangeAnalysisKind.title: ChangeAnalysisKind

ChangeAnalysisReport.description: The persisted, machine-readable rendering of one change analysis.
ChangeAnalysisReport.title: ChangeAnalysisReport

ChangeEvidenceItem.description:
One piece of analysis-scoped evidence, explicitly base- or target-side.

Unlike :class:`Evidence`, the analysis evidence model carries a ``side``
rather than a repository-wide ``snapshot_id``: the base side of a working
tree has no stored snapshot, only a commit, and pretending otherwise would
hide the historical nature of base-side citations.
ChangeEvidenceItem.title: ChangeEvidenceItem

ChangeKind.description: What happened to one symbol across a change.
ChangeKind.title: ChangeKind

ChangedFile.description: One file in the file-level diff.
ChangedFile.title: ChangedFile

ChangedSymbol.description:
One symbol that differs between the base and target states.

A deleted or moved-from symbol carries base line range and a base file path;
an added symbol carries target range; a modified symbol carries target
range and, when its content also moved, a base file path. The two are kept
consistent: base lines without a base file is a contradiction the contract
refuses, because a citation with no file is not a citation.
ChangedSymbol.title: ChangedSymbol

Conversation.description:
One persisted thread, always bound to a single repository.

A conversation never changes repository: switching requires a new thread
(Section 14.5), so a historical answer can never be reinterpreted against a
repository it did not examine.
Conversation.title: Conversation

ConversationPage.description: One page of conversations, newest activity first.
ConversationPage.title: ConversationPage

FileClassification.description: How a file participates in repository truth and impact analysis.
FileClassification.title: FileClassification

FileDetail.description: One file of the active snapshot, with its snapshot stated.
FileDetail.title: FileDetail

FileRecord.description: One file admitted into a snapshot.
FileRecord.title: FileRecord

ImpactEdge.description:
One edge in the impact graph, labeled but not cited.

An impact edge is a graph fact with a derivation and a confidence; it is
not a citable region of source. Keeping evidence off the edge is what keeps
the response's evidence list minimal and the exact/containing metrics
meaningful, per ADR-0003 and ADR-0005.
ImpactEdge.title: ImpactEdge

Message.description:
One turn in a conversation.

``sequence_number`` starts at 1 and orders the thread; it is also the
stream's resume key, so 0 is reserved to mean "nothing yet".
Message.title: Message

MessageEvidenceItem.description:
One citation attached to an assistant message.

The evidence fields are snapshotted rather than joined live: a historical
message must keep telling the truth it told after its snapshot is
superseded, which is the same audit rule change analyses follow.
MessageEvidenceItem.title: MessageEvidenceItem

MessagePage.description: One page of messages, in sequence order.
MessagePage.title: MessagePage

MessageStatus.description:
Where a message is in its lifecycle.

A failed or cancelled message stays visible and retryable; the states are
explicit rather than a boolean so partial and failed work can be told apart
from work that never started.
MessageStatus.title: MessageStatus

MessageSubmission.description:
The result of submitting one question.

Phase 5 answers deterministically and synchronously, so the submission
already carries the finished answer. The IDs are returned regardless of
outcome: a failed or cancelled turn is still a turn the client must be able
to display and retry.
MessageSubmission.title: MessageSubmission

OverallRisk.description:
The highest severity present in an analysis, or none.

Extends :class:`Severity` with one ``NONE`` value so an analysis with no
findings can still name its overall risk honestly rather than being absent.
OverallRisk.title: OverallRisk

RelationStep.description:
One edge of a relation path, citable on its own.

Every step carries its own evidence, so a path is auditable edge by edge
rather than as an opaque conclusion a reader has to take on faith.
RelationStep.title: RelationStep

SymbolDetail.description: One symbol of the active snapshot, with its file path resolved.
SymbolDetail.title: SymbolDetail

SymbolRecord.description: One symbol definition located in one file of one snapshot.
SymbolRecord.title: SymbolRecord

UpdateConversationRequest.description:
Rename, archive, or both. Unarchiving is not offered yet: nothing in
Phase 5 needs it, and an unused write path is an untested one.
UpdateConversationRequest.title: UpdateConversationRequest

WatchResponse.description:
Whether continuous freshness is on for a repository, and how it is doing.

`enabled` is the stored decision; `running` is the observed reality. They
disagree when a watcher could not start — a vanished directory, exhausted
handles — and showing only one of them would hide exactly that case.
WatchResponse.title: WatchResponse

WorkingTreeRequest.description: Analyze the working tree against a base ref.
WorkingTreeRequest.title: WorkingTreeRequest

get.description: Render a stored analysis. Every format reads the same persisted rows.

post.description:
Accept a question and return its IDs; the run answers in the background.

202, not 201: this acknowledges an accepted turn rather than presenting a
finished one (`CLAUDE.md` Section 12.2, ADR-0008). The user message and the
queued run are committed before this returns, so the IDs are durable and
the stream is already live — a client may open it immediately without
racing the worker. The persisted message stays authoritative; streamed text
is provisional.

get.description:
Stream the active run's events, resuming after the client's position.

Resume is accepted two ways because the browser leaves no choice:
`EventSource` cannot set request headers, so it cannot send
`Last-Event-ID` on the initial connection. The header is the standard and
wins when both are present; `?after=` is what a browser client can
actually use.
Re-verify a stored evidence region against the file on disk.

post.description:
Ask a run to stop.

202, not 204: cancellation is cooperative, so this acknowledges the request
rather than asserting the run has stopped. The run's own terminal event is
what says that.

schema.title: Response List Repositories V1 Repositories Get

get.description:
List the files the active snapshot contains.

Paths are repository-relative, as everywhere else: the absolute root is not
echoed back, so a screenshot or diagnostic bundle cannot leak it.

post.description:
Restore the previous snapshot as active.

The escape hatch for an activation that turned out to be wrong. With no
previous snapshot to return to this is a conflict, not a server error.

get.description: Report the watch switch and what the watcher is actually doing.

put.description:
Turn continuous freshness on or off for one repository.

The decision is persisted, so it survives a restart: turning the watcher off
is a statement about the repository, not about this process.
